articles.title: Rangers and Ryan Naderi finish off Celtic’s horror week with Old Firm victory
articles.summary: If ever a stadium can be rocked by silence, this was the moment. With no visiting fans allowed at any of this season’s Glasgow derbies, Ryan Naderi’s winning goal was met with nothing but the banging of fists of the clear plastic of the Rangers bench and the shouting of the broadcast commentators.
body: In the coming three weeks, as club football dissolves for the international break, noises and voices will pour into the void: some helpful and some not. This, of course, is a familiar feeling for any club of Celtic’s size, and naturally the temptation will be to block out the noise, stay the course. This would be a grave mistake. If last season’s double illustrated the way this club can still rise above adversity, there can no longer be any hiding place, no equivocation with the alarming drop in standards that was evident here.

Naderi’s goal, bundled in from close range after Kim Min-su’s long-range effort was parried helpfully into his path by Viljami Sinisalo, was simply the most consequential emblem of Rangers’ superiority here. Derek McInnes arrived with an unchanged team, coherent patterns of play, a functional and hungry midfield, order to their chaos. None of this has been remotely visible at Celtic for a while.

articles.title: GB reach Davis Cup Finals as Patten and Skupski win
articles.summary: Great Britain will play in the Davis Cup Finals for the first time since 2023 after taking an unassailable 3-0 lead against Ecuador in London.
body: Great Britain will play in November's Davis Cup Finals as Henry Patten and Neal Skuspki won their doubles match to give the nation an unassailable 3-0 lead in their qualifying tie against Ecuador.
Toby Samuel and Arthur Fery both triumphed in their singles matches at a sold-out Copper Box Arena in London on Saturday to get Britain off to a winning start in the best-of-five tie.

Patten and Skupski then took to the court on Sunday and booked Britain's ticket to the 'Final 8' event in Bologna at the earliest opportunity with a 6-3 6-4 win over Gonzalo Escobar and Diego Hidalgo.
It is the first time that Great Britain have reached the knockout stage of the competition since 2023.

articles.title: Patten and Skupski take Great Britain past Ecuador to reach Davis Cup Final 8
articles.summary: Pair win doubles match in straight sets. Finals are in Bologna in November. Few people across London enjoyed a more soothing night’s sleep than Leon Smith on Saturday.
body: In just their second match as partners rather than rivals, the world No 1, Henry Patten, and Neal Skupski, the US Open champion a week ago, played their roles to perfection as they convincingly sealed their place in the Davis Cup Final 8 with a clinical 6-3, 6-4 victory over Gonzalo Escobar and Diego Hidalgo, earning Great Britain an unassailable 3-0 lead. Harry Wendelken, the British No 7, closed out the tie with a 6-2, 6-3 win over Angel Veliz in the dead rubber.

The British team will next head to Bologna for the quarter-final knockout stage of the competition, which takes place between 24 and 29 November in the final week of the tennis season, for the first time since 2023. Their success in east London was dictated by wins on Saturday by Arthur Fery, the British No 1, and the No 5 Toby Samuel, who overcame tense starts before settling down and easing to victory.

articles.title: USA stun Ireland with comeback WXV win in Dublin
articles.summary: The United States stage a remarkable second-half comeback to beat Ireland 40-36 in their WXV Global Series opener at Tallaght Stadium.
body: Scott Bemand's side raced into a comfortable lead after 20 minutes following tries from Vicky Elmes Kinlan, Cliodhna Moloney-MacDonald and Aoife Wafer and went in 24-12 ahead at the break.

Erin King added a fifth try early in the second half as Ireland looked to be cruising at 31-12 up, but a loss of control and discipline aided USA, who under the guidance of their Irish head coach Jack Hanratty, managed to turn the game around.
Elmes Kinlan's yellow card was a turning point, with USA taking advantage of their numerical advantage as they scored four successive tries to take an unlikely win.

In the first women's rugby Test match to take place at the home of football team Shamrock Rovers, Ireland started with intent and, after persistent pressure, they made the breakthrough on seven minutes.

articles.title: Tottenham Hotspur injury blow confirmed after latest statement
articles.summary: Pedro Porro Injury Blow Leaves Tottenham Sweating Ahead of Key Run. Tottenham have another problem, and this one matters. Pedro Porro has pulled out of Spain duty after suffering an injury in the 3-2 home defeat to Aston Villa, adding fresh concern to a side already short on rhythm, points and fit…
body: Porro went down early in the game with what looked like a hamstring issue. He received treatment on the pitch, tried to continue, then came off in the 19th minute with Archie Gray replacing him. The reaction told its own story. He looked frustrated, hit the turf in anger and limped off with help from the medical staff.

For Tottenham, this is awkward timing. For Porro, it is worse. He had only just returned to regular action after an extended summer break following Spain’s World Cup success in North America. The Villa match was only his third start of the season, which underlines the bigger issue here, fitness management and recurring setbacks.

Roberto De Zerbi did not try to dress it up afterwards. “Listen, Pedro, I said after the World Cup, I said the management of Pedro should be different, because after the World Cup, many games. I don’t know what the problem is. It’s a hamstring, I think. Hopefully, it’s not a big problem.”

That is not a diagnosis, but it is enough to confirm the obvious. Spurs fear a proper lay-off and Spain have now lost him for the upcoming international window. No replacement has been called up, which says plenty about the timing and nature of the withdrawal.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark, Nike release behind-the-scenes video on signature shoe design
articles.summary: With her Caitlin 1s set to release to the public on Oct. 1, Nike unveiled a unique behind-the-scenes video highlighting the meticulous details of Caitlin Clark's shoe and the elements the former Hawkeye wanted to incorporate into its design.
body: The full video features Clark alongside Nike's Product Line Manager Alex Zerzan and Footwear Designer Ben Nethongkome, where the three-time WNBA All-Star describes exactly how she wants her first signature shoe to feel, look, and act for her and everyone wearing it.

The first half of the behind-the-scenes video shows several beneficial design elements Zerzan and Nethongkame used to meet Clark's desires for the shoe. Some of those components include the multidirectional traction blade pattern on the base, the responsive Nike Air Turbo Zoom unit near the front of the shoe, and the first-of-its-kind Opticast technology in the upper, to name a few.

"Caitlin is elite. She's an elite basketball player, and her standard when it comes to her footwear as well is elite also, and you know, I think she really pushed and challenged the team," Zerzan said. "What I love about working with Caitlin is she knows exactly what she wants, and you'll know if Caitlin likes something because it's immediate."

articles.title: DP World Tour plans to keep Play-Offs in UAE despite player safety concerns
articles.summary: DP World Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings has confirmed that the plan is to keep the season-ending Play-Offs in the Middle East, despite ongoing conflict in the region.
body: The Abu Dhabi Championship is scheduled to be held at Yas Links on November 5-8, before the Race to Dubai season reaches its climax at the DP World Tour Championship the following week.

There has been speculation throughout the season over whether both events would move to a different country, with Formula 1 cancelling two events earlier in the year in the region and discussions ongoing over whether races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi will go ahead.

Matt Fitzpatrick and Bob MacIntyre were among players to express concerns about travelling to the UAE, despite a relaxing of the previous "all but essential travel" guidelines from the UK's Foreign Office, with Kinnings hopeful both events can take place as planned.
"A lot of people are asking and it's an obvious question," Kinnings told Sky Sports. "The reality is we expect every intention to be playing in Abu Dhabi and Dubai.

body: Sunderland 's recent resurgence as a force to be reckoned with in the Premier League has been one of the feel-good stories in the top flight of English football.

And against Manchester City this afternoon, the Dutch international and former Ajax standout is putting together a one-off performance to remember, one week after he made himself out to be a nuisance against Arsenal at the Stadium of Light.

In doing so, Brobbey now sits alongside a handful of memorable figures and one outright club icon, becoming just the fifth Sunderland player to score a Premier League hat-trick, joining Kevin Phillips (two), Darren Bent, Jermain Defoe, and Adam Johnson.
Brobbey is also the first player to hit City on three occasions in a single match since Jamie Vardy back in September 2020, signaling his arrival as a true goal threat in the league.

articles.title: Rangers beat Celtic again to cut Premiership lead to two points
articles.summary: Ryan Naderi's strike gave Rangers their second win against Celtic in eight days to move within two points of their Old Firm rivals at the top of the Scottish Premiership.
body: Martin O'Neill had insisted Celtic's confidence was not "rock bottom" after their League Cup defeat at Ibrox was followed by a loss to Ferencvaros in the Europa League. But, in front of 60,000 of their own supporters, it certainly took another huge dent.
After Auston Trusty's effort was ruled out for offside, Rangers took the lead. Naderi fired in on the rebound after Viljami Sinisalo denied Min-Su Kim as the cheers turned to jeers at Parkhead.
Kieran Tierney hit the woodwork as the champions looked to respond, with Djedi Gassama then doing the same at the other end.
Celtic's first chance on target did not come until after half-time, but Ivor Pandur produced a huge save to keep Colby Donovan's header out.

articles.title: Broad excited at what Fleming can do for Root's captaincy
articles.summary: Sky Sports Cricket's Stuart Broad is excited at what new England Test coach Stephen Fleming can bring to Joe Root's captaincy as the New Zealander prepares for his first assignment in the role in South Africa this winter.
body: Fleming was named as countryman Brendon McCullum's successor in late July but did not lead the side for the recent 3-0 sweep of Pakistan due to family commitments.

The 53-year-old recently flew to England for a short trip to chat with ECB officials and Test skipper Root as well as the counties, and was with the national team as they completed a 3-0 T20I whitewash under white-ball coach McCullum in Manchester on Saturday.

Fleming - who has never been a head coach in red-ball cricket before but has extensive franchise-league experience, chiefly with Chennai Super Kings in the IPL - spoke to media ahead of the final T20I, including to Michael Atherton for the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast.
Broad said after listening to former New Zealand captain Fleming's chat with Atherton, in which he lauded Root: "What struck me was his love of leadership.
